A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QERA work. All 20 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning, post-training quantization, calibration and runtime results, including Tables I–IV and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds runtime/accuracy comparisons, LoRA rank sweeps and further activation-correlation analyses.

M1.justification: The QERA-exact and QERA-approx objectives, activation scaling, truncated-SVD solutions and low-rank reconstruction procedures remain unchanged. The CALDERA discussion establishes a claimed connection rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: The datasets and tasks are retained. New runtime and rank studies reuse MRPC, SST2 and SlimPajama. Additional model configurations in the activation analysis do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmarks retain full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, LoftQ, BF16, w-only, ZeroQuant-V2, LQER and HQQ as applicable. Added internal comparisons reuse QERA-exact and QERA-approx; CALDERA is discussed through theoretical equivalence, without a separately reported implementation.

E3.justification: New appendix experiments vary rank and training duration while measuring initialization, training and total time. Tables 9–10 sweep LoRA ranks 4–20 and learning rates 1e-4–6e-4. These add bounded evaluation protocols; the original benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.8 adds experiments testing whether initialization savings can support additional rank or training and improve final quality. A.9 adds empirical rank-sensitivity studies supporting the previously qualitative over-parameterization argument. A.11 expands the displayed assumption checks beyond the retained LLaMA-3 plots to LLaMA-2, Mistral and TinyLlama.

E5.justification: Both versions report fine-tuning results averaged over seeds 42, 1 and 2. V2 adds no documented change to repeated-run practices, confidence intervals, significance testing or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All matched original tables retain their numerical entries, but Tables 7–10 add substantive runtime, accuracy, perplexity and rank-sensitivity results. Examples include rank-16 QERA-exact at 6.31 perplexity and 6.8 hours on SlimPajama, and LoRA rank-12 accuracies of 94.73 on SST2 and 89.95 on MRPC. Expanded correlation plots add further findings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds optimization formulations and an explicit derivation claiming equivalence between QERA-exact and CALDERA’s Lemma 4.2, beyond the retained Theorems 1–2. The new derivation contains inconsistencies: Equation (37) conflicts with the defined symmetric square root, and Equations (36)–(37) use inconsistent singular-value inverse factors.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the analytical-framework and QPEFT/PTQ improvement claims, including the 6.05-point GLUE gain and 2.97-point PTQ accuracy gain. Added supporting analyses do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.8 explicitly recommends QERA-approx for fine-tuning and QERA-exact for PTQ, explaining initialization cost, recovery through training and unchanged inference form. A.9 strengthens the over-parameterization interpretation with rank-sweep evidence. Earlier calibration and numerical-stability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-and-model repository link, clarifies that learning-rate selection is performed for each method/task pair, and supplies settings and timing breakdowns for the new controls. Existing hardware, software and quantization implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds CALDERA as closely related concurrent work and acknowledges an equivalent exact solution, replacing v1’s assertion that no work provides an analytical solution. Section 2 and Appendix A.3 substantially refine novelty positioning through different optimization variables and QERA’s approximate solution.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. V2 makes local wording and citation edits, adds acknowledgments, revises subsection organization and moves the extended assumption discussion to the appendix’s end.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially resizes and regroups displays. It adds a notation table, four experimental tables and twelve correlation figures. Existing calibration, scalability and correlation figures are retained and relocated; detailed PTQ tables are consolidated.

improvement.justification: The new runtime and rank studies better substantiate practical choices that v1 largely motivated qualitatively. Broader assumption checks, explicit CALDERA positioning and the code/model access link also improve usefulness. These provide a modest net gain, tempered by algebraic inconsistencies in the added equivalence derivation (Equations (36)–(37)). Those defects affect the new connection argument; the original QERA theorems and benchmark evidence remain intact.
